observations: O1 (for Robin, requirement conflict): V2's delta 'USB mouth X in [-1.8, -0.8]' cannot be met together with L2.1.6/L3.1.6.1 (Pico pins on the board grid) using the catalogue data: perfboard part.json gives a 90 x 45 board a grid starting at X 5.63 (grid_margin_x 4.74, centred), rpi_pico2 part.json puts pin 1 at 1.37 from the USB edge and the receptacle 1.3 past it, so the mouth is at 5.63 - 1.37 - 1.3 = 2.96 at the closest on-grid pose. The delta looks stale (it fits a grid starting near X 1.4). The plug still seats with 0.40 mm clearance through the 2.4 mm wall at this pose. Grade kept as written: FAIL. If Robin confirms the analogue of E1-01's rule ('first pin on grid column 0, +/- 0.5', i.e. mouth X in [2.46, 3.46]), this design passes every applicable L3 and MEETS.

O2: Jacks connector_1_1 and connector_1_2 (bodies X 21-27 and 42-48, Y 0-12, Z 0-5) touch the Pico PCB's long edge at Y = 12.000 (Pico PCB Z 2.5-3.5, component keep-out to Z 5.0) with zero clearance. Interference volume 0.0 mm3, so L3.1.4.1 passes, but there is no assembly tolerance; the PJ-320A drawing body is 12.2 long (catalogue 12.0), so a real jack would overlap the Pico by about 0.2 mm. Visible in ghost_top.png where the red and green jack bodies meet the purple Pico rectangle.

O3: Tight-but-passing margins: top and bottom keep-out 0.10 mm, USB and jack plug clearance 0.40 vs 0.30, boss pilot depth 6.10 vs 6.0, standoff pilot depth 5.10 vs 5.0, lip engagement 2.10 vs 2.0, standoff OD 5.10 vs 5.0.

O4: The corner bosses (dia 6.6 at (-3.29, -3.29) etc.) stick out from the box corners (model_iso.png, all four corners) and intrude about 0.2 mm into each cavity corner (at (-1.1, -1.1) etc.). The lid lip has a dia 7.11 notch around each one (0.25 clearance) and stays one continuous ring. They are not defects.
O5: Each standoff (OD 5.10 at 2.5 from the board edges) reaches 0.05 mm past the board edge (X/Y = -0.05 or 90.05 / 45.05). It is harmless and inside the V-SEAT columns.
O6: The jack openings (dia 8.81 at Z 2.5) go down to Z -1.905, below the board's underside (-1.6), so the board edge shows through the openings (model_front.png). No L3 covers this.
